slides.title: Thinking, Feelings, and Imagination
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 3 English, Unit 9: Thinking, Feelings, and Imagination. This unit explores the world inside your head: thinking, feeling and imagining. You will learn sixteen words for ideas and emotions, including idea, sense, reason, sadness and experience. You will practise imagining, making a choice, giving a reason with because, and suggesting ideas kindly in a group. In the story The Box of Ideas, children at a school by the sea fill a special box with their dreams and hopes. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use abstract nouns like idea, reason, experience, and sadness to talk about thoughts and feelings.
Say what you imagine and describe the pictures in your mind.
Give a reason for something using because.
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use abstract nouns like idea, reason, experience, and sadness to talk about thoughts and feelings. You will also say what you imagine and describe the pictures in your mind. You will also give a reason for something using because. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Words to learn
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: idea, imagine, reason, purpose, choice, sense. Listen to each word, look at what it means, and try to use it when you talk and write.

slides.title: Read and think
bullets: The Box of Ideas at School
Feelings Are Not Bad or Good
Point to the words that show it
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes The Box of Ideas at School and Feelings Are Not Bad or Good. Read slowly, look at the pictures, and find the big idea in each text. When you answer a question, point to the words that show it.

slides.title: Abstract Nouns
bullets: An abstract noun names something you cannot see, touch, or hold, such as a feeling, a quality, or an idea. Words like idea, experience, sadness and...
Try it in your own sentences
slides.narration: The first language focus is Abstract Nouns. An abstract noun names something you cannot see, touch, or hold, such as a feeling, a quality, or an idea. Words like idea, experience, sadness and kindness are all abstract nouns. They let you talk about what is happening inside your mind and heart. Look at the examples, then try the pattern in your own sentences.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Writing 1 — My Idea for the Box
Say it, write it, make it better
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1 — Share an Idea. Say your ideas clearly and listen to your partner. In writing, you will draw, trace, copy or write, then check your work with a grown-up or the AI tutor.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the words, then the reading and the questions, then the grammar, speaking and writing. Ask the AI tutor for help any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
